one_liner: Pure-Rust SIMD crypto, hash and Base64 crate that edges OpenSSL AES-128-GCM on ARM but ties it on x86; unaudited.
what_it_does: A git-only crate named tachyon (version 0.1.0). It covers AES-128/256 in ECB, CBC, CTR and GCM; ChaCha20, Poly1305 and ChaCha20-Poly1305; GHASH/GMAC; MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-512 and BLAKE3; HMAC and HKDF; and Base64, all written with core::arch intrinsics. Its API is its own, not a drop-in for OpenSSL EVP or ring. For example, AES128Gcm::from_slice(&key) followed by encrypt_slice_detached(&nonce, aad, &mut buf, &mut tag) encrypts in place with a detached tag, and md5::compute(data) or Sha1::new().update().finalize() hash.
how_it_is_fast: Each primitive has hand-written intrinsics per instruction set. On x86 that covers SSE2, AVX, AVX2 and AVX-512: GCM uses VAES and VPCLMULQDQ, Poly1305 uses AVX-512 IFMA with 44-bit limbs, and ChaCha20 has an AVX-512 path. On ARM it uses NEON with the ARMv8 AES and PMULL instructions. A 6-block GHASH path (build.rs cfg ghash_block_x6) is enabled on x86 and Apple aarch64. ChaCha20-Poly1305 interleaves the stream cipher with Poly1305 over 16 or 64 blocks at a time. Without target-feature flags, union-based Dynamic types dispatch at runtime. Chips without AES instructions fall back to RustCrypto's fixsliced software AES.
when_to_use: Bulk AES-128-GCM on Apple or Snapdragon CPUs, in experiments or code you will audit yourself. README: A16 9225 vs OpenSSL 7330 MiB/s (1.26x), Snapdragon 888 1.20x, M4 1.11x at 64 KiB.
Non-cryptographic MD5 checksums: 1-17% above OpenSSL on 9 of 10 platforms (Ryzen 9 9950X 1289 vs 1187 MiB/s, RPi4 326 vs 279) and up to 1.8x the md5 crate.
Legacy SHA-1 in Rust: 1.7x to 6.7x ring's SHA-1 (M1 2301 vs 343 MiB/s).
Base64 encoding of large buffers: README shows 2.3x to 4.6x the base64 and data-encoding crates (M4 26433 vs 5805 MiB/s), but the repo has no bench target for this table.
As readable, MIT OR Apache-2.0 reference code for intrinsics-based AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305 and BLAKE3 kernels in Rust.
when_not_to_use: Production TLS, storage or messaging encryption: the README says the library is not formally audited, is meant for benchmarking and experimentation, and should not be used in production.
AES-GCM on modern x86: it ties OpenSSL on the Ryzen 9 9950X (33179 vs 33121 MiB/s), so it offers nothing over OpenSSL or an OpenSSL-backed crate there.

ChaCha20-Poly1305 on Apple silicon with a stable default build: 27-37% slower than OpenSSL and ring (M1 1148 vs 1816 MiB/s); only a nightly -Ztune-cpu=generic build wins. On the i7-3770 it is also behind ring.
BLAKE3 on x86 or RPi4: the official blake3 1.8.2 crate is faster (Ryzen Z1 Extreme 8364 vs 8096 MiB/s, Ryzen 9 9950X 13441 vs 13348).
When you need a crates.io release, semver, a documented MSRV or documented constant-time guarantees: none exist, and Cargo.toml pins most dependencies as '*'.

integration.dependencies: cfg-if, unsafe_target_feature ('*'), libc ('*'), the in-repo path crates tachyon-macros and optional instr_hex; build dependencies rustc_version ('*') and cfg_aliases. Git dependency only.
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 2021 edition on stable; AVX-512 paths need Rust 1.89+ or nightly (build.rs); the Apple ChaCha20 win needs nightly -Ztune-cpu=generic; MSRV not documented
integration.platforms: x86-64 (SSE2 to AVX-512 with runtime dispatch) and aarch64 (NEON plus AES/PMULL) per the README; the code also has 32-bit x86 and arm cfgs and portable software fallbacks
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. Cipher and hash objects are plain owned values. The Dynamic dispatch types lazily initialise unsynchronised `static mut` index globals (for example IDX in aes/dynamic.rs) on first new(). Commit 992ce47 (2026-07-26) narrowed a race there by storing the index once, but the accesses are still not atomic.

gotchas: Poly1305 is not RFC 8439 Poly1305 when used on its own: update() (scalar mod.rs and x86_avx512.rs) zero-pads a partial final block and sets the 2^128 bit, which is the AEAD pad16 rule. As a standalone MAC it therefore gives different tags for messages that are not a multiple of 16 bytes, and since there is no internal buffer, each update() call pads independently. It is only correct inside the bundled ChaCha20-Poly1305.

Harness flaw (correctness): the Ryzen 9 9950X and Z1 Extreme ChaCha20-Poly1305 rows (README commit e171231, 2026-03-23; 9950X rose from 4121 to 7576 MiB/s) were measured on an AVX-512 IFMA Poly1305 added 2026-03-21/22. Until commit 09c2cb6 (2026-03-31), that code applied raw-Poly1305 0x01 padding instead of pad16, so tags were wrong whenever AAD or message length was not a multiple of 16 bytes. The 64 KiB, empty-AAD benchmark never reaches that branch, and the benches never check their output.

The OpenSSL column is cross-run and stale. Commit e171231 changed only tachyon cells and ea37614 (2026-03-31) changed only tachyon and ring cells. The OpenSSL cells (mixed versions 3.2.1 to 3.6.1) were not re-measured alongside, and no repo code produces them. Only the ring and md5-crate comparisons are same-run Criterion measurements, and even those run against unpinned '*' versions with no Cargo.lock.

Fixed correctness bugs in less-tested paths: the 32-bit software AES (fixslicing32.rs, used only when target_pointer_width is 32) emitted its output words in the wrong order until commit 5e51145 (2026-06-01). CI runs `cargo test` only on 64-bit ubuntu-latest and ubuntu-24.04-arm runners. AVX-512 paths are tested only where the runner's CPU has them. The crates.io name `tachyon` belongs to an unrelated crate (nh13/tachyon), so `cargo add tachyon` without --git installs the wrong package.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Only two catalogued siblings overlap: Usuba (a compiler emitting bitsliced C for AES-CTR and similar primitives) and the Zig base64 entry. Pick tachyon for AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305 or Base64 inside a Rust program on ARM, and only after your own audit. Pick Usuba for constant-time bitsliced kernels in C. For production Rust crypto, ring or OpenSSL remain the safer choice.
verified_claims_summary: First-party README tables give single-call 64 KiB throughput in MiB/s on 11 CPUs. AES-128-GCM beats OpenSSL 3.2.1 to 3.5.0 by 3-26% on Apple and Snapdragon (M4 12212 vs 11043), by 12% on the Ryzen Z1 Extreme and by 2.4x on an RPi4 software path, and ties on the Ryzen 9 9950X (33179 vs 33121). ChaCha20-Poly1305 beats OpenSSL 3.4.1 on the 9950X (7576 vs 6900) but trails it on Apple chips in the default build. Only the ring and md5-crate columns come from the repo's Criterion benches (opt-level 3, fat LTO, codegen-units 1); the rustc version and target-cpu are not stated.
status_note: Active single-author project (205 commits, last 2026-09-18, 4 stars, no issues or releases), dual MIT/Apache-2.0 and so copyable, but git-only and self-declared unaudited; its OpenSSL comparisons are cross-run, and its x86 ChaCha20 numbers predate an AVX-512 Poly1305 tag fix.
